notes: AUDIT CORRECTION: the dense/sparse flag was inconsistent with this record's own note. 74 (TF32) and 148 (BF16/FP16) are the DENSE values and are now flagged dense:true; 296 (FP8/INT8) remains the SPARSE figure per flopper.io. Note the whole record is still third-party-sourced (status draft, vendor_claim false on every row) because NVIDIA has never published an H20 datasheet. LOWEST-CONFIDENCE RECORD IN THIS SET, deliberately. NVIDIA has never published a full public H20 datasheet: H20 is the export-restricted Hopper part whose compute was cut to satisfy US export controls while its memory subsystem was left generous. I could not reach a primary NVIDIA spec table for it (resources.nvidia.com's HGX H20 doc is a JS PDF viewer with no extractable text; nvidianews.com carries only the PR). Every figure here comes from Flopper.io, a third-party aggregator, so vendor_claim is set FALSE on all rows and status is draft, not verified. The shape of the part is the interesting bit: 148 dense FP16 TFLOPS against 96GB at 4.0 TB/s. That is roughly 2/3 of H100 SXM's dense 989 TFLOPS but a HIGHER bandwidth-per-FLOP ratio, so H20 is a memory-rich, compute-poor Hopper - the opposite trade from H100. The FP8/INT8 296 figure is the sparse number per the source, so dense would be 148. Bus width is inferred, not sourced.
